notes.title: Join the Eastward: Octopia charity livestream with Lomadiah!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Next week we've got something very special lined up for you all - an [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2305370/Eastward__Octopia/]Eastward: Octopia[/url]-themed charity livestream supporting [url=https://foodcycle.org.uk/]FoodCycle[/url] 🧡 

On [b]April 18th at 14:00-19:00 BST[/b], we’re teaming up with the amazing Hannah Rutherford, aka [url=https://www.twitch.tv/lomadiah]Lomadiah[/url], on her Twitch channel for the #PlayforPlates fundraiser! Check out the [url=https://tiltify.com/@lomadiah/plates]Tiltify fundraising page[/url] to get involved. 

Our only-one-in-the-world Eastward auction item is also now live on eBay, once again with all net proceeds from the sale going to charity: [url=https://www.ebay.co.uk/itm/145728301380]https://www.ebay.co.uk/itm/145728301380[/url]

[h2]What's 'Play for Plates'?[/h2]
With Eastward's new DLC seeing John and Sam embracing a peaceful new life in the countryside, what better timing than to team-up to raise funds for the fight against food waste and food poverty. 

Hannah ‘[url=https://www.twitch.tv/lomadiah]Lomadiah[/url]’ Rutherford, who you might also know for her fantastic fundraising work, is kindly working with us to host the charity livestream to benefit FoodCycle, a remarkable organisation that has been spreading warmth and nourishment in the UK since 2009.

[previewyoutube=8sKkdxnTDIs;full][/previewyoutube]

FoodCycle's story is about community, compassion, and care. They take surplus food and turn it into hearty meals for those who need it most by creating spaces where people can come together, share a meal, and feel a sense of belonging. It's a recipe for change, and we're proud to be a part of it. 🌱🥕

Her passion and dedication to supporting non-profit organizations are truly inspiring, and her community is equally committed to these causes. We couldn't have asked for a better match to join us in this initiative!

notes.title: Eastward: Octopia DLC - Available Now!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Today is the day! Get ready to trade in John's bang-bang gun for a watering can, and embark on a tranquil new life in Octopia. (Don't worry, you'll still need that frying pan 🍳).

In [b]Eastward: Octopia[/b], Sam and John return in a parallel world adventure, leaving the miasma and monsters behind them, to start a simpler life, living off the land. 

[previewyoutube=CvLxStBALgQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Eastward: Octopia is available for $5.99 / £4.99 / €5.89 / 700円 / ¥22 CNY, with a special launch offer of 15% off the DLC running from today until February 14th! We're also running special limited-time offers on the base game & bundle too.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2305370/Eastward__Octopia/

🌏 Playable in English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese, and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/2cd03436811c001177ce3be585a9bced4e3ef84f.png[/img]

[h2][b]💰 Is there a launch discount?[/b][/h2]
Eastward: Octopia is available for [b]$5.99 / £4.99 / €5.89[/b], with a special launch offer of [b]15% off[/b] the DLC running from today until February 14th!

The Eastward base game is also on sale at [b]40% off[/b], and if you haven't started your Eastward journey yet there's a [url=https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/36902/Eastward__Between_Two_Worlds_Bundle]discounted Bundle[/url] available too! The Bundle is also available with the discounts included so there's no better time to jump in!

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/36902/Eastward__Between_Two_Worlds_Bundle

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/68b6510c2f9ab4bf4c4b540faee3174e3a9aad4e.gif[/img]

♨ Lead a peaceful new life: Help Sam and John cultivate a life free from worries. Say goodbye to the chaos of the outside world and immerse yourself in a countryside haven.
 
🌾 Revitalise the farmstead: Roll up your sleeves and breathe life back into a neglected cottage and its lands. Grow crops, rear (and pet!) adorable animals, forage in the wetlands, wind down with some fishing, and even strike up a conversation with a friendly ghost.

💗 Build a thriving community: Construct and upgrade stores and homes to transform Octopia into a bustling community. Complete culinary requests to attract more familiar faces to the area — some might decide to make Octopia their permanent home!

🍳 Culinary Delights: Utilise farm-fresh ingredients and John's Cookbook to whip up delicious recipes. Invite your neighbours to dinner to share your culinary creations and build connections over the universal language of good food.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/224c1d08642a539346e8da304fe698af5f75c14c.gif[/img]

[h2][b]🎮 What platforms is the DLC available on?[/b][/h2]
Eastward: Octopia is now available on Steam and [url=https://www.nintendo.com/us/store/products/eastward-octopia-70050000042973-switch/]Nintendo Switch[/url]. 

[i]An important note regarding the NS physical version - please ensure you purchase the DLC from the same eShop region as the base game in order for the DLC to activate. If you purchased a physical copy of Eastward, please check which region it is before you download the DLC product.[/i]

In terms of other platforms where the Eastward base game is currently available, the dev team are looking into making the DLC available and we will update the community as soon as we have more news.

Did you know that Eastward is also fully verified for play on SteamDeck? We think Eastward: Octopia is the perfect game to take with you on the go!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/85f730887a9d8169ad44c7489fef85385d978c52.jpg[/img]

[h2][b]🐣 Do I need to have played the Eastward base game before I play the DLC? [/b][/h2]

Eastward: Octopia takes place in a parallel universe, so there's no need to have finished (or even started) Eastward's base game story to enjoy the simple life - you can even play it straight from the main menu. 

Although many familiar faces appear in Eastward: Octopia, the plot, gameplay and character 'settings' will be a completely new experience.

[u]However, please note that a copy of Eastward is required to access the DLC. [/u]

Once you've purchased and downloaded the DLC, make sure the DLC is 'checked' in the base game properties. After starting the base game of Eastward in your Steam Library, you can then travel to the pastoral time and space of Eastward: Octopia is a single click from the main menu interface!🚞

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/0091fe65e102d850001f245aa6885a757adb9fad.png[/img]

Eastward and the Eastward: Octopia DLC each have their own independent multi-save location. This means that when you need a break from the bustling streets of New Dam City, you can jump back in the DLC where you left off for some rural tranquillity in Octopia (or vice versa)! Although the stories unfold in parallel, experiencing the two completely different lives of the protagonists at the same time might also help to unearth some easter egg links that will make you smile! 😄

[h2][b]⏰ How long is the DLC?[/b][/h2]

We estimate that it will take about 15 to 20 hours to clear the main content of the DLC, but the actual time depends on your playstyle. Some players may spend more time discovering recipes to unlock and make various tasty dishes 🍛, or get re-acquainted with familiar characters! You might also indulge more time in mini-games such as fishing 🎣 or the bomb-mining game. It's safe to say there is much to be discovered!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/d89941cc3831ded77f9b875d56d35697d6ab6505.gif[/img]

⏩ We have also added the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/977880/view/3870344877704851791]"fast forward" function from the recent December base game QoL update[/url]. When playing animations and talking to characters, players can press the E key to speed up and skip text passages; or they can take a nap on the bench in front of John & Sam's cottage to recover their physical strength while the in-game time speeds up.

[h2][b]📖 Any tips for how to get started in Eastward: Octopia?[/b][/h2]
A successful life in the countryside always starts with getting hold of some good farm tools and getting to work planting and harvesting crops, clearing the fields, and selling your produce! Last week we posted a Steam News blog all about Farm Management tips - take a look!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/977880/view/6507196838848385990]https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/977880/view/6507196838848385990[/url]

You can also bring up the game menu at any time to view the current cooking tasks, find out the location of town residents on the map, check crop information and maturity time, and gradually unlock more character information. Videos demonstrating farming, harvesting, felling etc. in the game are also shown in the Settings menu.

[h2][b]Love Eastward? How about some super-duper-exclusive merch? 🤩[/b][/h2]
Now available for pre-order is the 'Eastward: Design Works' collection, including music, prints, and a stunning 250-page masterpiece of an artbook, all created in collaboration with our pals from Lost in Cult. 

There are 2 different editions to choose from, including the 'New Dam City Deluxe Edition' featuring a beautiful spot-gloss hardcover, yellow slipcase and outer box, section sewn binding, art prints, A3 posters, enamel pin badges, a cute 'saving memories' Fridge bookmark, a set of Eastward culinary recipe cards + an Earth Born zine! The first 500 copies of the New Dam City version will also include a bookplate attached to the inside, signed by the dev team at Pixpil. 

The Eastward: Design Works is expected to ship in Summer 2024.

[url=https://www.lostincult.co.uk/eastward-mobile]Check the Lost in Cult website to grab yours before the campaign ends on Feb 14th![/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/6aa6dbfb6eb32af9ea1e2160eb307a112a930c09.png[/img]

We're beyond excited for you to embrace the simplicity and joy that await in Eastward: Octopia. Thanks to each of you who supported and got excited about this new project with Pixpil! 

We hope you have a blast! 🌱🎣🍲✨

notes.title: Entering Octopia: A Guide to Farm Development
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It's only a few days to go now until the release of [b]Eastward: Octopia DLC on January 31st[/b]! 

As a reminder it's coming to Steam and Nintendo Switch first, and is priced at [b]$5.99 / £4.99 / €5.89 / 700円 / ¥22 CNY[/b]. It will be playable in English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, French, German, and Spanish!

Although the pastoral life in Octopia is leisurely and comfortable, as farmers, John and Sam still need to work hard to turn their muddy fields into bountiful harvests. In order to restore prosperity to the town, we have prepared a guide to farm management and land reclamation for you ahead of your stay in Octopia:

[h2][b]Cultivation, Exploration, and Hard Work![/b] 🌾🐣[/h2]
In this parallel universe of Eastward, you’ll find a beautiful pixel art world free from miasma and monster invasions. Instead waiting for you beyond the train station gates is a small town ready to be renovated and a rundown farm desperately in need of some TLC. 

First step? Clear away all of that the rubble and weeds, and sow some colourful seeds instead! On sunny days you’ll need to irrigate your crops with your handy unlimited watering can, and once they’re ready pop on your gloves to harvest them with one click.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/c0307d05acc6dcb73de29bd5ce2396af40ce9747.gif[/img]

In addition to the half-acre field at your doorstep, the town also has other ecological wonders waiting to be discovered - woods, wetlands, beaches… Use various tools to crush rocks and chop trees to collect building materials, and find special resources - perhaps you'll encounter something that can be used as ingredients for cooking or sold at William’s shop - every natural gift can be put to good use!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/20bac54bccf75b00af566fc4b15559b311c2bd78.jpg[/img]

Of course all tasks require a bit of effort to be done properly - from sowing seeds, to chopping and watering tasks, each mechanic reduces the energy bar in the lower left corner of the screen. You can restore your vitality with a good sleep and some of John’s amazing cooking. In the early stages of the game, food and money may be a little scarce, so it’s important to think carefully about ‘economical’ farm work, and how you will best spend your day. 

For example, a secret to making a fortune quickly might be in planting crops with short harvest times, or grinding grains to sell in William’s shop for higher rewards. When you're ready to lay down your tools for a while, John and Sam can sit on the bench in front of your home to watch the day roll by, and slowly regain energy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/30da07dfb95065e852999b5742690562afd82dfa.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Recipe Creativity & Ingredient Preparation[/b] 🍳🥗[/h2]
In comparison with the travelling adventures in the base Eastward game, John’s time in Octopia sees his finally having a chance to improve his cooking skills, creating and studying the preparation of new recipes and rich specialties. As you spend more time in Octopia, you will discover special recipes based on different ingredients through thought-bubble association. 

You can then harvest, forage or source these ingredients to combine and cook delicacies from the mountains and seas. For example, think of rice and shrimp together, and you'll get a delicious new recipe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/ec703a0e7a497b9b0b058bf06c8c51fcf09e0ea7.gif[/img]

Food doesn't only restore the physical strength of John and Sam, but also furthers the story of Octopia and its inhabitants. Throughout your journey you’ll spot familiar faces from Eastward’s base game, but they might look a little different this time around and act in unexpected ways in their new life in Octopia... Some things never change though, and certainly not these character's foodie nature - so if you want to get to know their stories, you’ll first need to sate their appetites! 

Preparing ingredients is also a key part of cooking: foraging in the wetlands and rivers, planning planting according to the maturity and harvesting times of different crops, and ordering seeds and stock from the store in advance of running out of stock… It all adds up! 

But remember the best way to celebrate many days of busy work on the farm is to invite all of your friends around for dinner and share stories across the table while eating delicious home-cooked meals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/132d5d63c016e7597ea37b94c39bb169b0268d15.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Fishing time! [/b]🎣🐡[/h2]
Octopia is full of rivers and ponds, making it an absolute paradise for budding anglers. But this might not be fishing like you know it - long gone are the days of swinging the rod to reel in the line, putting down the bobber and waiting for a hungry fish to take the bait. 

In Octopia fishing is about speed and strength! Fish will race in a circle, so you’ll need to pull up the rod at the exact moment you catch up with their shadow. Some agile fish species may require a few more attempts! If you’re too slow, the fish will break free from the line and escape back into the waterways.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/17398c4e03dc84ee36ecbf786f3e2a730ed3ff14.gif[/img]

Not only is fishing a way to spend some time away from the farm, but in the early stages of the game it can also be a great way to obtain cooking ingredients without expending too much energy, or can be turned into a tidy profit if sold in the store.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/29f5cf823b38f9a86a0a432d3e877c94e7b3760a.gif[/img]

In addition to your farm’s nearby ponds, you can also explore new fishing areas as the town develops. Different types of fish require different physical strength and can also be more difficult to fish. By choosing a variety of baits, you can reel in unexpected catches - even if you happen to catch a roll of toilet paper, it might have other ‘convenient’ uses!

[h2][b]Resources, Upgrades & Construction[/b] 🏗👷‍♂️[/h2]
When you first arrive in Octopia it looks a little bit… unloved. Well fear not! By cutting down rocks and chopping trees to collect building materials, you will gradually be able to build new facilities, such as stores, pastures and even laboratories, slowly transforming Octopia to its former vibrancy! 

Collecting resources will require some time and effort, but keep in mind that upgrading daily farming tools can achieve twice the result with half that effort. For example, upgrading your watering can and fishing rod in the store and through shrines can greatly improve the efficiency of your crop watering and fishing adventures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/b51d958bd586386ef95e53fc1f8a82c141393209.gif[/img]

As the story progresses, you will unlock the underground mine area! Similar to the visual style of Earthborn, the mining mini-game in the Octopia DLC is inspired by retro arcade machines. Various precious ore resources can be mined by bomb explosions, which can be used to upgrade more practical tools and building facilities. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/beec9d0319bc20394bd14f5c427625374a67a2ed.gif[/img]

That’s it for our short introduction to farm management in Eastward: Octopia! We hope it will help you settle into your new rural town life when the DLC launches next week. (There's also still plenty of secrets and easter eggs waiting to be discovered!) notes.title: Announcing Octopia - a new farming DLC, coming to Eastward!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/87196f8207f3e5e43f20b9602ec850644517b01c.png[/img]

Hi everyone!

I bet you didn’t see that coming 👩‍🌾🌾♨

Today we’re super excited to announce that Sam and John will be returning in an all-new adventure, coming to the wonderful world of Eastward. Octopia is the start of their peaceful new life in the countryside - no miasma, no hardships, just happy times and delicious meals.

[i](Psst, haven’t finished playing Eastward yet? Don’t worry, the Eastward: Octopia DLC will be accessible straight from Eastward’s start menu, and suitable for brand new players and Eastward completionists alike.)[/i]

[h3]Check out the all-new Octopia announcement trailer here:[/h3]

[previewyoutube=COCIcZI0Q1s;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]🚂 Next stop... Octopia![/h3]

In a parallel world, Sam and John alight from their train at a remote station in a mountainside village, ready to start their lives anew. The duo decide to spend all of their savings on a rundown farm cottage, desperately in need of some TLC. All the best things in life come with a little hard work and elbow grease! 

[h3]🌾 A New Life in the Countryside[/h3]

In Eastward: Octopia, you’ll help Sam and John to work the land, tend to their blimpigs, and cook heartwarming meals for familiar - yet strangely different - friends. Upgrade your farmstead, grow crops, forage in the wetlands, get advice from friendly ghosts, and spend your nights casting your line in the local fishing holes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/a4f6931dd748332fc17b4cdc288f21385e5071bf.gif[/img]

[h3]🛠 Revitalize a Community[/h3]

When Sam and John first arrive the town of Seagull looks a little … neglected? But don’t worry, you can revitalise the community by helping to construct homes for new neighbours, upgrade stores and encourage even more familiar faces to flock to the area with the help of your farm-fresh ingredients and cooking prowess. 

But even in these quiet lands, there are secrets still waiting to be discovered…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/b92fb01f719a0b6c1a54c3e8e4759cd97e468316.png[/img]
[i]Crops, ghosts, and blimpigs oh my![/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/05e19647b395d38d0886d6134e83dbc3eee2cb3b.png[/img]
[i]Help bring the best out of the town![/i]

This is a sizable paid DLC for Eastward, with a brand-new story and an all-new farming game mode. You will need the Eastward base game in order to access the Eastward: Octopia DLC. It will be playable in English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese, Simplified and Traditional Chinese.

The development team at Pixpil has been secretly working on Octopia since Eastward launched nearly 2 years ago today, so we’re incredibly excited to see what you all think! We’re currently aiming to launch the DLC on Steam and Nintendo Switch this Winter - more news on that as the final stages of development progress.

[b][u]Q&A[/u][/b]
[i]🌾 Is the Octopia DLC a brand new game mode?[/i]
Yes! Unlike Sam and John’s post-apocalyptic adventure filled with fighting off monsters and tricky puzzles, Octopia will show a slice of a peaceful new life in the countryside - no miasma, no hardships, just happy times and delicious meals.

[i]🐣 What is the connection between Octopia and the world of Eastward?[/i]
Octopia’s story takes place in a parallel world, completely different from the main game. There’s no miasma or dangerous mutant creatures 👾 here - instead, an abandoned farm awaits John and Sam to start their life anew. Familiar and different companions from Eastward will visit with new ideals and goals, working together to help the town thrive!

[i]⏰ How long is the content of the DLC expected to be?[/i]
We estimate that it will take at least 15 to 20 hours to complete the main content, but the actual duration depends on your playing habits - many players may spend more time studying recipes to make all kinds of dishes 🍛, getting to know characters, enjoying their time with companions, mastering the art of fishing 🎣 or blasting away in the mining mini game. Octopia also has its own secrets to share…

[i]🌱 When is the DLC expected to be released?[/i]
Octopia will release on Steam and Nintendo Switch this Winter. The bulk of the development is complete, and the studio is continuing to polish, fix bugs 🛠 and optimise the experience. We hope to share the specific release date as soon as possible!

Eastward will be going on sale very soon with its deepest discount yet at 50% off - so keep your eyes peeled for news when the sale period starts!

Until next time!

notes.title: Designing Earth Born
notes.content:
Hey everybody! Since the launch of Eastward on PC & Switch, we’ve loved seeing so many of our community members discover and fall in love with Eastward’s not-so-hidden inner RPG (within an RPG) Earth Born, so we thought it was a great time to share it’s development story and secrets! 

Since the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/977880/view/3056248229761372024]v1.1.0 update[/url] Earth Born is now also accessible from Eastward’s menu after you’ve completed the game. So, boot up your console and blow off your memory card, because we’re going to be talking about Earth Born...

[i]*fair warning, if you’ve not played yet, there may be spoilers ahead*[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/71a5d321e5ef33f8f8fbb0489fa22b33f4391357.png[/img]

[h2][b]Retro Origins[/b][/h2]
The idea of Earth Born first sparked from the dev team’s desire to create a cultural grounding (or something memeable) that linked all of Eastward’s in-game towns and cities, something which connected all of the characters despite the horrors of the miasma and the divisions it created. The art would reflect the world around the characters in Eastward and add a (not-so) fictional context to the realities that players face throughout the game. The deeper you dive into Earth Born, the more fun parallels you may start to notice! 

Earth Born also acts as a homage to the Pixpil team’s favourite games, comic books and movies; [i]Dragon Quest, Porco Rosso, Cowboy Beebop[/i]. The name ‘Earth Born’ comes from Eastward's initial Chinese project name '大地之子,' which means 'The Child of the Earth’ - a nod to the [i]Earthbound[/i] series which had inspired them to create games in the first place!

[b]Fun Fact #1: [/b]Did you know after you complete your first run of Earth Born, you unlock [url=https://twitter.com/pixpilgames/status/1439490367536046080]different screen modes[/url]?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/8d4f3eddcde856f7ed90668da7e060c6cc104eb6.jpg[/img]

[h2][b]Taking Down the Demon King[/b][/h2]
Earth Born is a retro-inspired, turn-based RPG roguelite. It’s first introduced as the most popular video game in all of Potcrock Isle (and Sam’s favourite)! You have 7 in-game days to thwart the Demon King who’s bunkered down in a castle at the center of the map, before the world is swallowed up by a great darkness!

However, at the start of the game, your party isn't nearly strong enough to take him on. Players will have to do multiple runs to visit inns, recruit new party members and activate the bird portals across the map in order to stand a chance. You’ll need all the help you can get when facing the Demon King...

Players must earn as much experience as possible to level up, ready for the big fight. Cave exploration is highly beneficial as players can gain more experience and acquire better equipment here. And of course, if you are struggling with a battle, gathering more Pixballs before you boot up to use will certainly help!

You can find more strategy, stats and tips in the [url=https://eastwardwiki.com/Earth_Born]Official Eastward Wiki[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/b56f40b0210519f16be62946eec667d734440d2c.gif[/img]

[h2][b]Okay, but what about the Pixballs?[/b][/h2]
As fans of collecting figurines themselves, Pixpil wanted to create something in-game tapped into the Amiibo / Pop Vinyl culture. Pixballs are acquired via Japanese-style gashapon machines which use arcade tokens to operate, found tucked away all over the map. It wasn’t until later into development that it was decided that Pixballs would have an impact on gameplay by creating powerful in-game items for players to boost their chances of winning.

[b]Fun fact #2: [/b]Pixpil’s favourite Pixball monster is the Gull Swordsman! Try saving your chips from this avian warrior!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/52d4418a2181ba1a66b6189f2a7c31afbcf2b7a7.png[/img]

When booting up an Earth Born arcade unit you can also access the in-game manual! Pixpil are quite rightly incredibly proud of the manual, written from the perspective of the in-game Earth Born developers. It’s a beautiful tribute to the detailed manuals of RPGs of old, brimming with nostalgia. But did you know that there’s an easter egg on the first page that nobody has mentioned yet? If you’re a fan of old school RPGs and you get the reference, let us know!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/e33432b8fa9e8c362ce22b11136b486352d54866.png[/img]

If, like us, you’ve had the Eastward soundtrack on repeat, you might be pleased to know that the Earth Borne soundtrack by Yu Fang is [url=https://yufang900809.bandcamp.com/album/earthborn-soundtrack]available on Bandcamp[/url]! You can also follow their musical journey over on Twitter too!

[previewyoutube=ktddB0Ps0TI;full][/previewyoutube]

Don’t forget we also have amazing merch including t-shirts, pins, posters and plushies, available now with [url=https://www.fangamer.com/collections/eastward]Fangamer[/url] and [url=https://theyetee.com/collections/eastward]The Yetee[/url]! We also recently announced a really awesome long-sleeve ‘Travel Tee’ and a cute ‘Saving Memories’ acrylic standee to [url=https://theyetee.com/collections/eastward]The Yetee store[/url] which would make for totally cute gifts this holiday season.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/ef3a076f49e06ff4247f0988b7abef8383a6a66f.jpg[/img]

That’s all for now. If you haven’t already come and join the community discussion over on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/chucklefish]Discord[/url] or [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/eastward/]Reddit[/url], and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ChucklefishLTD]Twitter[/url] for more Chucklefish gaming news.

Our team at Chucklefish will soon be signing off for Christmas, but we’ll be back with more awesome Eastward news in the new year. Until then, have a wonderful holiday break and take care!

notes.title: Update 1.1.0
notes.content:
Greetings, dear Earth Borners! It’s been just over a month since Eastward was released on PC and Nintendo Switch and we wanted to update you on all the work we’ve been doing since then. Many of you might have reached the end of your journey already, and also been kicking evil demon butt in Earth Born, but rest assured we’ve been listening to your suggestions and feedback, and we optimized many key issues in this new update. Let’s get right to it!  

[h2]New Features:[/h2]
[b]Chapter Selection has now been added to the Main Menu.[/b] Many players told us that they would like a second trip across the continent, so we’ve added a new option on the Main Menu which unlocks once you complete your first playthrough. This will allow you to select the Chapter you want to experience again or collect something you missed the first time around. You can now start a new journey from a specific Chapter, and have the option to carry over items and other content from your previous saves.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/abd01c79998113bce6517573e06316db5565b61d.png[/img]

[b]Run Earth Born directly from the Main Menu.[/b] We’ve added Earth Born to the main menu! After your first playthrough, you can continue to play Earth Born with the Pixball date of your current saves. Check out this additional option in the ‘Extras’ menu!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/d0e947e77e569929df39cabf2da3331834efd2d0.gif[/img]

[b]Fast Travel Function Unlocked.[/b] Here comes the Eastward express! We know that players have been busy exploring the world on foot. To help you on your current journey, or to revisit the beauty of the locales and towns in Eastward, we’ve set up Fast Travel points— once you trigger certain checkmarks in the story, these travel points will become unlocked. Whether you are a newcomer or an experienced adventurer, everyone should enjoy this quality of life improvement.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/7fc0277ab796317e1e59f5159c3ede124b4e2513.png[/img]

[b]New Graphics Modes Available.[/b] We have been listening to player feedback about the game’s native resolution, which has one of our main focuses in this update. As we have promised, Eastward now has a “high resolution” UI available. In the Filter Mode option, three different modes are available, including a “Clear Mode” (with crisp unfiltered graphics) and a fun “CRT Mode” for retro gaming lovers.

The first time new players launch Eastward, they’ll be prompted to choose their preferred graphic mode; or this can be changed anytime can via in-game Settings. Here are preview images of the three different graphic styles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/dae09f0603463a72a22b5b8cb6d41723eaa34d1e.png[/img]
(Clear Mode)
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/3d45fd59c1bfa1f5ad3eb624cfd92199c10b5444.png[/img]
(Normal Mode)
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/bcbedbcd5c9ed6dc3efa2088d71ac26378e4955e.png[/img]
(CRT Mode)

Alongside these new features, we’ve also fixed a number of issues reported by the community in this update, including the inability to collect all Pixballs, game crashes, lagging, and other bugs. If you encounter any problems while playing Eastward, please join the Chucklefish Discord channel or let us know on the steam forums.

Below is an extensive list of everything Pixpil have been working on - please be aware there may be some slight spoilers:

[h2]New Features:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fast Travel on the map 
[*] A new option on the Main Menu after the first playthrough, which includes：
[*] Chapter Selection: Start a new game from a specific Chapter with an empty save or a load data from a previous Chapter selection save.
[*] Earth Born: Play directly from the menu, and collect data from your existing save 
[*] Play Credits
[*] A Display Mode selection option appears at the first launch of the game 
[*] New filter mode (Available in Clear, CRT, and Normal)
[*] Added mapping for the Right Analog Stick function
[*] Added a map opening reminder at the beginning of the first Chapter 
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fix for John's raft becoming stuck when he crosses the gate and returns in a scene in the forest south of Greenberg
[*] Fix for when the characters are on the edge of the manual lift and road, their positions can be wrong after players operate the device and switch characters quickly
[*] Fix for characters being able to walk on the water

notes.title: 2 Weeks of Eastward
notes.content:
Hello again! Can you believe 2 weeks have flown by already? And WOW what an amazing 2 weeks it’s been. We’re absolutely thrilled with the community’s reception of Eastward and delighted that so many of you have already embarked on this weird and wonderful adventure with Sam and John. Thanks to each and every one of you who have supported the team at Pixpil and picked up a copy of Eastward - it means the world. Alright, gooey bit over.

[h2]Patches on the Horizon[/h2]

We wanted to quickly address the current known bugs that the team is working on fixing. We appreciate those who took the time to send us reports, feedback and information on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/977880/discussions/0/2954914054176692380/]Steam Forums[/url], [url=http://www.discord.gg/chucklefish]Discord[/url], [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/eastward/]Reddit[/url] and everywhere else. Pixpil are currently working on a larger patch which will address a number of the bigger issues:
[list]
[*] Launching & black screen issues
[*] General data-leak crashes
[*] Cursor getting stuck
[*] Earthborn menu locks
[*] Offline mode support
[*] Rendering / fps issues with Xbox controllers
[*] John & Sam entering ‘out-of-bounds’ areas
[*] + other reported higher priority bugs
[/list]
Switch-specific Bug:
[list]
[*] Friendly Spendie & King Krab shop softlocks
[/list]

We’ve noticed a few players commenting about features which are already in the game, such as text speed options, so please check the in-game menu settings posting change requests! Several bugs and feature changes have already been resolved in post-launch patches, full Version History and patch notes can be found on the [url=https://eastwardwiki.com/Version_History]Official Eastward Wiki[/url].

As we’re a small team we can’t always reply to every post, but we do read them all! If you’re a Nintendo Switch player, you may see patches release a few days later than on Steam due to the longer submission process, but rest assured they are in the works and on their way! 

[h2]QoL Updates[/h2]

Following some important bug fixes, we will be moving on to QoL (quality of life) updates. So far we’re looking at adding the following features based on your community feedback:
[list]
[*] Higher resolution menu UI
[*] Sharper resolution for enlarged scaling output
[*] Fast-travelling in town areas (via the Map). Please note this will take some time to test to ensure players don’t miss important story triggers.
[*] Chapter Select for New Game+ for players who want to get all optional elements!
[*] Earthborn to be playable from the menu once player has completed the Main Story
[*] PlayStation controller UI
[*] Other minor tweaks such as more Salt drops
[/list]
We can’t give an estimation of how long each of these features will take, as all will need thorough testing and localisation, but we will let you know how they’re coming along. If you have any other suggestions, please post them on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/977880/discussions/0/]Steam Forums[/url] or the [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/eastward/]Eastward subreddit[/url] which we check regularly.

Another hotly requested update from the community is of course more localisation support for Eastward! Now that the game is out we will be reviewing the demand before we confirm which additional languages will be added. As Eastward is a story-based game, there’s a lot of text to be translated (approx 143,000 words) so please be patient as adding further language support may take some time to ensure high quality!

Finally, we wanted to briefly address the comments around the game’s resolution. While Eastward is a pixel art game, it’s not actually 2D at all, [url=https://twitter.com/pixpilgames/status/1420710628319133699]but in fact 3D with a 2D perspective[/url]! It’s how the Pixpil dev team has been able to achieve such a unique atmosphere, with the addition of shader textures and lighting systems in their custom engine. You might notice when you play layers of fog, or brilliant sunbeams casting down on the landscape at various points throughout the game day. Each pixel and bespoke lighting detail was handcrafted and took a lot of time to create, but we think our players appreciate the small things! 

While Eastward is natively a 720p output, a baseline the dev team decided on early in the process, because of the intricate lighting techniques it can’t be simply ‘scaled up’ easily in a standard ratio like other pixel games. As mentioned we are also currently working on a patch to add a higher-res UI and a sharper resolution for larger outputs, which we hope will please the PC player community! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/2d1fcf52495bed890401d3663d9b9a26b182d750.png[/img]

[h2]Glimmer - OST Track[/h2]
We know many of you have been enjoying bopping along to Joel Corelitz’s awesome soundtrack as you discover more of the wide world of Eastward, so here’s another music video for you - Glimmer!
https://youtu.be/e0DhUYABgn0
You can pick up the whole soundtrack [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1586600/Eastward_Soundtrack/]here[/url] on Steam, or over on Joel’s [url=https://joelcorelitz.bandcamp.com/album/eastward-original-soundtrack]Bandcamp[/url].
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1586600/Eastward_Soundtrack/

[h2]More Lovely Fan Art![/h2]

We’ve loved seeing how much wonderful fanart has been shared in the past few days - here’s some more of our favourites~

That’s all for now. If you haven’t already come and join the community discussion over on our [url=http://www.discord.gg/chucklefish]Discord[/url] or [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/eastward/]Reddit[/url], and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ChucklefishLTD]Twitter[/url] for more Chucklefish gaming news.

notes.title: Winter Development Update - New Screenshots!
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

I hope you’re all staying nice and cosy as we edge into December, or chilling out in the sunshine for those of you in the Southern hemisphere. 

It’s been a hot minute since we last updated you about the progress of [b]Eastward[/b] and it’s no secret that this year has been a tough one for everyone, including the developers at [url=http://www.pixpil.com/][b]Pixpil[/b][/url]. The team in Shanghai lost access to their server for quite some time at the beginning of the year, with the power cut to their office and no way to enter the building at all due to quarantine restrictions, which of course had some knock-on implications to the development schedule. However fantastic progress has been made despite these challenges throughout the year, and Pixpil are now working on Eastward’s final chapter segment, tightening some loose ends and brushing up a few boss battles. 

It’s all super exciting stuff, and we can’t wait to show you more in the coming months. Even though we won’t have the game ready before the end of 2020, we’ll be ramping up our communication about the game as it gets closer to release - there’s certainly plenty to talk about! 

To kick off this new blog series we wanted to show you all a few new screenshots and introduce you to a little more of the weird and wonderful world of Eastward. If you’re dead set on avoiding spoilers then look away now! 

Okay, still here? Let’s go!

[i](Please note: Some place & item names may change)[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/5aceb5c02416c2b6673ba7e523eb753fc5485843.png[/img]

In John’s mining hometown of Potcrock Isle, inhabitants have spent their whole lives beneath the earth’s surface with no knowledge of the outside world!  In front of Hello Grocery store you can see a gacha machine and Earth Born arcade unit, where you’ll be able to play Sam’s favourite monster-collecting JRPG. We’ll show you more of that soon!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/72e2bc74311b5f70e832d160efdffde837252c72.png[/img]

Welcome to Greenberg, a laid-back idyllic village tucked away in the middle of a forest. You’ll pass through these golden fields during the annual harvest time, and get the chance to meet some friendly locals! I’m personally a huge fan of how each of the village homes are constructed from rusting landlocked ships, some complete with their own majestic duck. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/f48c2967528301b10e28d03fbbe539fe507aba06.png[/img]

Not long after arriving in Damhill, the city’s food market will open, giving you access to a variety of exotic cooking ingredients (sandrupes and fire mints anyone?) as well as a notorious sewage system. Cooking is an integral part of Eastward’s gameplay, with lots of delicacies to discover and strange recipes to try out with various health, power and other secret bonuses - we’ll post a blog in the future to explain more about how it works!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/b389646aa1dbc88761101f32460a8fb7188df001.png[/img]

Throughout their adventure, Sam and John will be boarding a cross-country railway as they travel eastward [i](hehe)[/i] through the decaying landscape. But some stations and tracks need a little fixing up before they’re fully operational... 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/33911849/928275e8ceaefcc8c8c05691b4d37b4cd79a3309.png[/img]

When you need to take a break from the hustle and bustle of city life in Damhill you can always take the train to this beautiful old bath house for a quick and relaxing dip. It’s run by a cute older couple who seem like they may also moonlight as passionate tomato farmers.

Eastward was also recently shown in a Japanese [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TA2cRwURmWM&feature=youtu.be&t=7360]INDIE Live Expo II video showcase[/url] alongside many other fantastic indies - check out the video that was shown below!

[previewyoutube=Xk4yFfasFs0;full][/previewyoutube]

Alright, that’s all for now. We’ve got much more lined up for you all as we approach the final stretch before launch. If you haven’t already, make sure you add Eastward to your Steam wishlist to get notified about the latest developments! 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/977880/Eastward/

If you’re a streamer and keen to get early access to keys when they’re available you can request access by filling in our [url=https://bit.ly/ContentCreatorForm]Content Creator form[/url]. You’ll also find answers and basic info about the game in our [url=https://eastwardgame.com/faq/]handy FAQ[/url].

Lastly, if you're as excited about Eastward as we are, come join the community discussion over on our [url=https://discord.com/invite/XgcZrm7]Discord[/url] or [url=https://www.reddit.com/r/eastward/]Reddit[/url], and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/ChucklefishLTD]Twitter[/url] for more Chucklefish gaming news.

Happy Holidays everyone!
-Chucklefish

notes.title: Eastward Demo Available Now For Only 48 Hours!
notes.content:
Hey everybody,

Superconsole here from Chucklefish! We’ve got some exciting news for you today… 

A few weeks ago Valve approached us to ask if we’d like Eastward to participate in their special game demo event, to which we of course said “hell yes!”.

From NOW until the next *approx* [b]48hrs only[/b], we’ll be providing Steam players exclusive access to a snippet of two gameplay sections from Eastward, giving you an exciting glimpse into the gameplay and characters...

[list]
[*] Explore a beautiful (yet slightly dilapidated) town
[*] Chat to quirky townsfolk
[*] Peep inside tiny shops
[*] Adventure through a strange forest
[*] Battle unusual monsters, like the bomb duck!
[*] Switch between frying pan melee attacks with John and Sam’s telekinetic powers
[*] Solve environment and dungeon puzzles
[*] Defeat a mini boss!
[/list]

Please keep in mind when playing this demo, that it’s currently a work in progress, so you may encounter small bugs, features not yet fully implemented (such as cooking and hints) or incomplete localization. 

If you do encounter an issue or would like to share your thoughts and feedback on the demo, please feel free to comment on this thread to let us know!
